location: p. 37, Findings: Replication of previous study; p. 42, Appendix B
quote:
The first study with just college
students appeared to show that the greater webpage background complexity had a
negative effect on those attitude variables. In contrast, the second study with no college

reason: The shipped 'successful' quote on p. 39 concerns the hierarchy-of-effects hypothesis (H1) rather than webpage background complexity. However, the blind 'failed' verdict is also not effect-specific to attention to the commercial (ATT_ad): in the original study (Stevenson, Bruner, and Kumar, 2000, p. 32, Table 1 and Discussion), background complexity already had no significant effect on attention (F = .522, p = .595; 'the backgrounds did not appear to make a significant difference in the attention that subjects reported paying to the commercial'), while the replication's H2 MANOVA (F10,152 = .57, p = .84, p. 37) and Appendix B statement (p. 42) evaluate five outcomes jointly and explicitly refer back to Study 1's negative effect 'on those attitude variables' without providing an attention-specific replication verdict.
